newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Poland stresses wants full NATO membership.
newsitem.headline: Poland stresses wants full NATO membership.

text.p: Poland's Defence Minister said on Tuesday his country was aiming for full membership of NATO in 1999, stressing that Poland did not want second class status.

"For us it is very important to become a NATO member but not a second class member. We want to be a full member of NATO," Stanislaw Dobrzanski told reporters, adding he anticipated that would be in 1999.
He was in The Hague to co-sign an agreement with Dutch Defence Minister Joris Voorhoeve, finalising joint manoeuvres in which 3,500 Dutch troops will take part next month.
Poland has been anxious that NATO should not agree on a watered-down NATO membership for new entrants to meet Russian objections that the pact's enlargement threatens its security.

At their Helsinki summit last Friday, U.S. president Bill Clinton and Russia's Boris Yeltsin agreed to disagree on NATO's expansion plans but vowed to press ahead with a charter to set a new relationship between Russia and the 16-nation alliance.
Voorhoeve said he expected to see a charter in the coming months that would spell out the role of Russia in managing Europe's security. "We need a charter like that anyway," he said.
"The entry of Poland and other central European states into NATO is not aimed against anybody who is not a member. Russia is a friend of NATO," added Voorhoeve.

Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary are leading candidates to be invited to begin membership negotiations at the NATO summit in Madrid in July, with the aim of joining in time for the alliance's 50th anniversary in 1999.
